products_text: Established in 2019, the 700-bush Anderson Berry Farm operates on a foundation of environmental stewardship and high-quality fruit production. The blueberry bushes are irrigated exclusively with well water and maintained without the use of pesticides or herbicides. To ensure optimal plant health, wood chips are applied regularly to the base of the bushes to manage pH levels, retain moisture, and provide natural nutrients. This care extends into the winter months, when annual pruning in January promotes fresh growth and to remove old branches. The result is a premium harvest of blueberries available for U-pick or pre-picked orders from May 25th through July 4th.

Arrowhead Acres is a small pick your own blueberry farm located in upstate SC just off Highway 414 in the beautiful foothills of Travelers Rest. The farm is family owned and operated since 1980. products_text: I want to be the first person in South Carolina to farm duckweed for human consumption. Duckweed is high in protein, vitamin B-12, and anti-oxidants. Duckweed is native to South Carolina and looks like a microgreen. It has a fresh look and earthy smell, a neutral to slight peppery flavor, and a delicate texture. My duckweed is grown on John’s Island in a clean, hydroponic environment inside a greenhouse where I closely monitor everything that goes into and comes out of the system. products_text: Farming isn’t just a business; it’s a way of life. Our farm was co-founded by three generations of our family: our grandparents, Bruce & Linda; our parents, Bryan & Kelly; and us, Nick & Taylor. Our farm is a haven of tradition, hard work, and a deep-rooted connection to the land. Our farm name, Faith and Freedom Farm, is also a tribute to our dad’s military service in the United States Air Force. His commitment to our country and his dedication to serving others has shaped the values that drive our farm and family. We believe that tending to the land and caring for our animals is not only a responsibility but a blessing. We offer fresh and nutritious Microgreens! Microgreens are young, tender greens that pack a powerful punch of flavor and nutrition. These tiny, vibrant plants are harvested just a few weeks after germination, making them exceptionally tender and bursting with intense flavors. But it’s not just about taste – our microgreens are also packed with essential nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants. Despite their small size, they are known to contain higher nutrient levels compared to their mature counterparts, making them an excellent addition to any balanced diet. Whether you’re a professional chef looking to elevate your dishes with a burst of color and flavor, or a health-conscious individual seeking to add a nutritious boost to your salads, sandwiches, or smoothies, our microgreens are the perfect choice. Grown with care and precision in our controlled environment, our microgreens are pesticide-free and harvested at the peak of freshness. We offer a wide variety of microgreens, including but not limited to spicy salad, broccoli, cilantro, radish, and sunflower and pea sprouts, each with its own unique taste profile. Experience the freshness and nutritional benefits of our microgreens by visiting our website and placing an order online. We guarantee that each bite will leave you craving more!

products_text: Honee mecca is a vessel to holistic wellness in our community. Our mission is to change how we approach our well-being and self-care by promoting transparency, inviting our community to share helpful remedies, diversity and nuturing habits that enhance not only our skin but our overall health. We offer a range of products crafted from high-quality organic, wildcrafted, and locally sourced fair-trade materials, including salts, clays, oils, butters, herbs, flowers, and resins, mainly sourced from supporting local farmers, artisans, herbalists, and beekeepers. By collaborating with these creators, we help maintain traditional crafts and sustainable farming all designed to reconnect with nature, support inner healing and taking charge of our health.

We offer horse riding lessons, toddler equine exposure sessions, farm camps, private tours, birthday parties, field trips, music/art/storytelling classes, agriculture lessons through Farm School and photography sessions. We have a large variety of animals including horse s, pony, goats, sheep, alpaca, llama, pig, mini horse , mini mule, mini cows, hedgehogs, chickens, ducks, turkeys, peacocks, guinea fowl, geese, emu, rhea, bunnies, cats and a dog. We sell farm fresh eggs, pet bunnies, pet hedgehogs and sheep. **Our farm is open by PRIVATE APPOINTMENT ONLY. Please do not arrive and expect service without a previously scheduled appointment.** We have a farm shop open to the public daily from 10:00am-7:00pm. The Farm Depot is our farm shop at Horse Crossing Farm. We are a SC Certified Roadside Market! The shop is stocked with locally sourced items such as eggs, baked goods, tallow, jams, vintage farm toys/decor, manure/compost bags, goat soap, organic candles, crafts, handmade jewelry, etc. Here is a list of the services that we currently offer at the farm! The majority of lessons will involve riding, but not every single lesson. We teach our students not only how to ride, but everything else they need for horse ownership and care. We offer Western and English lessons. Ages 5+ No prior horse experience required Semi-private: Lesson groups of 2-4 students $40 an hour lesson Lessons are held once a week and are booked and paid for one month at a time. products_text: Litt Lizzy Farms is a veteran owned, minority owned and woman owned farm located near Leesville, SC. We organically produce fruits like melons, grapes, and strawberries. We also grow vegetables including beans, corn, okra, and other staples of the southern dinner table. We are also a South Carolina Department of Agriculture permitted industrial hemp farmer since 2022. Once our hemp varieties are grown and processed we make products targeted to customers who are seeking alternative pain or stress relief from hemp’s many healing properties. Our customer base includes households seeking fresh, affordable, locally grown produce and also those seeking safe effective ways to maintain good health. The history of our farm includes the determination and diligence of the owner’s grandparents, Andrew and Essie Quattlebaum, who first purchased more than 100 acres during the early 20th century. They preserved through many years of strife and hardship but successfully farmed the land and reared their many children and grandchildren. Today we are dedicated to continue the legacy of the ancestors by tending the soil and taking good care of what has been handed down to us, proudly upholding the legacy of the small family farm.

We offer U-Pick strawberries, blueberries, and blackberries in the spring and early summer, and a pumpkin patch in the fall. Comments from a visitor on August 01, 2010: "We found this farm/property from signs posted on Highway 130 heading up to the North Carolina mountains this weekend. The owner, Paul, is eager to get the word out and does not know how to do it. (I would not be surprised if he did not have internet access.) From my memory, I'd say it was around Salem, SC but because it was my first drive up this way, I'm not sure. The property was less than a mile off of the state road. What we loved about the property was that it is all "organic" though not officially. The only thing he uses to grow his rows and rows of mature bushes is rainwater. He'll never get enough traffic for all of his blueberries to pick and he's begging for people to come so that the birds do not get all of the spoils. Paul was as nice and friendly as could be. He provided the white picking buckets and charged us $9/bucket, which was very reasonable. (We used the same buckets at Southern Belle Farm here in Georgia and paid $10 per for strawberries.) I could have picked all day if my three kids weren't hot and hungry after an hour. He provided us with water to drink and my five-year-old even helped him prune some of his bushes. The blueberries are amazing. My two-year-old kept picking and eating! This farm was the only one we saw as a "pick-your-own" on this road. Paul has a sign right at the left turn-off off of 130 that takes you to a quick left turn to get to his property. We were doubtful since it was an instantaneous decision but once we came to the property and met Paul and his blueberries, we were thrilled beyond belief. I should have gotten more info from him but our kids were shot and ready for some lunch so we ended up making a quick exit. Hope you can find his location. He's eager to get the word out and he has so many mature blueberries that I hope others, other than the immediate locals, can enjoy them too!"

products_text: There are seven acres of land in Dacusville, South Carolina we call Rambling Rosa Farm. The land is Cherokee. Recently it was a horse farm. In relationship with it we are growing Rambling Rosa, a diversified vegetable + herb market garden farm. The way we grow our vegetable and herb crops is guided by health principles. This means we respect and try to enhance, not interfere, with natural processes in the soil. It means no sprays or chemical fertilizers (it also means we’ll be applying for organic certification). While the crops are growing, we also feed and look after friendly farm animals that have arrived here through adoptions from the humane society and other local farms. products_text: The South Carolina Botanical Garden (SCBG) is the state botanical garden of South Carolina. Our vision is to be a regionally recognized demonstration site for best practices in horticulture and conservation through excellence in natural resource stewardship, horticultural practices in the built environment and visitor engagement. As a holistic garden, we strive to provide an excellent example to the public of resource-wise, healthy landscapes that foster diversity. We are committed to providing a center for learning and promoting our southeastern native plants, as well as those plants that provide valuable ecosystem services and are well-adapted and resource-wise in our managed landscapes. We are committed to controlling and reducing the negative impact of invasive species in our ecosystem. Our nursery is an integral part of the Garden. The nursery grows high-quality plants to support both the gardens and, in turn, the public community. The nursery hosts the Garden’s Semiannual Plant Sales (typically in April and September or October) and produces plants for sale through our gift shop and events across the state. Plants are also grown for research, restoration, outreach, conservation and our display collections. SCBG produces a wide range of nursery crops including annuals, herbaceous perennials and woody perennials (trees and shrubs).

products_text: Swamp Rabbit Cafe and Grocery – FOOD HUB In 2016 we identified a huge need in our community and were ready to take local food to the next level, through helping farmers further market and sell their crops, and helping other businesses source local. Most small farmers aren’t able to deliver to 100 different restaurants, but food hubs are. Most restaurants aren’t able to order from 100 different farmers, but food hubs are. So, what do we do? We crop plan with growers to help them grow crops with high market demand, in the right quantities, at the right time, and we commit to selling those crops on their behalf. We do more than just market their products: we tell these producers’ stories to restaurants, grocery stores, and other food hubs. We provide post-harvest handling education, resources, and supplies. We aggregate demand, coordinate weekly harvests and deliveries with our growers, and once it reaches our door, we tackle the logistics behind transporting local food from one end of the state to the other, and beyond!; farmers-market

products_text: Villacado Farm is a family operated farm in Camden, South Carolina, offering premium products and immersive experiences that celebrate land, livestock, and local artistry. We specialize in sustainability grown specialty crops for U-pick visitors, pasture-raised premium goat and pork, chicken, duck, and guinea fowl eggs. Beyond what we grow, Villacado Farm is a vibrant natural space. Guests can enjoy private farm tours, guided seasonal U-pick produce, live music events, art showcases, goat yoga, baby-goat bottle-feeding sessions and even paint-and-pick art classes. Every event is designed to bring people closer to the land and offer a memorable, hands-on connection to local agriculture. At the heart of everything we do is a commitment to preserving soil health, honoring natural cycles, and raising animals and crops in a way that strengthens the ecosystem for generations to come. To maintain the tranquility of the farm and the wellbeing of our animals, ALL VISITS are by appointment only. We’re always available to help with scheduling or answer any questions about the farm through our listed contact information. For seasonal releases, event announcements, and behind-the-scenes glimpses of farm life, follow us on social media and stay connected with the Villacado community.
